children: , Google's advertising, cloud and AI powerhouse, backed its biggest carbon-removal project yet, Reuters reported Wednesday. Shares slipped approximately 0.9% to $341.72, even as Google pushed deeper into technology designed to offset the growing environmental footprint of its sprawling AI infrastructure.

Terradot plans to deploy enhanced-weathering material across more than 200,000 hectares of rice fields in Brazil, targeting one million metric tons of methane-abatement credits by 2030 and another one million tons of carbon-removal credits by 2040. That removal target is roughly ten times the scale of earlier rock-weathering projects. Google already owns an equity stake in Terradot, giving it exposure not just as a buyer of credits but as a financial backer of the technology itself.

The economics are where this gets interesting. A 2024 Terradot transaction implied a removal cost of about $300 per ton, while developers see roughly $100 as a level that could unlock much broader adoption. Pricing for Google's latest agreement has not been disclosed, so investors cannot yet calculate the direct financial return. Meanwhile, the valuation picture is already demanding: Alphabet's $341.72 share price stands 34.54% above its GF Value estimate of $253.99. That gap puts more pressure on Google's massive AI and infrastructure spending to translate into durable growth rather than simply bigger capital commitments.

title: Alphabet Gains as Carbon Removal Scales Tenfold
